overview: The commission accepted a demolition application for 7 Hamlin Avenue and addressed several year-end administrative tasks. Members approved the 2023 meeting schedule, reappointed the current slate of officers, and discussed ongoing budget and grant challenges.

items.title: 7 Hamlin Avenue Demolition Application
items.summary: The commission accepted the demolition application as to form and approved spending $500 for a Form B research report.

items.title: 31 South Street
items.summary: This item was continued to January because the required legal advertisement was not published in time.

items.title: Agenda Procedures and Annual Report
items.summary: Following legal advice, the commission will remove specific times from future agendas to allow for more flexibility, and members began planning the 2022 annual report.

items.title: Reimbursements
items.summary: Approved a reimbursement of $75.18 for postage and archival supplies.

items.title: 2023 Meeting Schedule and Community Outreach
items.summary: The commission approved the 2023 meeting calendar, which includes a contingency date in October to handle demolition business within the 30-day regulatory window.

items.title: Officer Elections and Subcommittee Appointments
items.summary: The commission reappointed the existing slate of officers for 2023, designated members to the website and archives subcommittees, and reappointed Doug Carr to the Community Preservation Committee.

items.title: Project and Budget Updates
items.summary: Members reviewed renovation progress at 130 Boston Avenue and discussed difficulties with the municipal finance department regarding multi-year grant funding.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes from the November meeting.
